narrative.overview:
FlowLight has two surfaces with one job each, and they read as one product. Operators work in a light administration framed by a graphite sidebar: an overview that says what is ready and what is missing, lists whose first column shows the thing itself (a game's cover, a player's initial, a line's icon) with its state in a dotted pill, and a side drawer for editing so the list stays in view. Players use a dark native Windows client that sits beside a running game, usually in the evening: a game library rather than a settings form. Generated cover art opens each game, region and line choices are tiles and rows that carry their own evidence, and one round dial starts acceleration and then becomes the live latency readout.

The client's material is warm graphite with a faint violet cast, separated by tone rather than outlines and lit by a single amber, the "flowing light" of the product's name. The administration borrows that material instead of inventing its own: its sidebar is the client's window graphite, its work area a lilac-tinted white whose surfaces lift on a soft shadow rather than an outline, and the same amber marks its brand, actions, selection and focus. On both surfaces latency, health and publication state speak in a separate green, orange, red and blue set. Pictures carry recognition: cover art drawn per game from a hue and a few light streaks (the same hue for the same game on both surfaces), outline icons on one 24 px grid, four signal bars, a latency chart. No game artwork is bundled, and no figure appears without saying what it measures.
keyCharacteristics: One product, one amber: a light administration in a graphite frame and a dark graphite client; amber is brand, action, selection and focus on both, never state.

Administration: 248 px graphite sidebar grouped 配置 / 账号 / 运行, an overview of four metric tiles and a 上线准备 checklist, card lists with entity first columns and row actions, side-drawer editors, and phone layouts down to stacked row cards.
Client: 80 DIP icon rail, a library of 16:9 cover cards, a game page with a hero banner, region tiles, line rows and the dial.
A game's generated cover takes the same hue in both apps, from a cover slot fixed when the game is first stored.
Every client figure is a probe with a visible provenance label; missing evidence is an em dash.
Unknown, draft, unavailable, refused, historical and current states remain explicit.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the brand, the action, the selection and keyboard focus, on both surfaces, and nothing else. It never reports quality or state: latency, load, connection, publication and health speak only in green, orange, red and blue.

rules.name: The State-Tone Rule
rules.body: In the administration a tone is a reading, never decoration. A pill shows a dot and a word, so colour is never the only signal; an overview tile's icon badge is green when its count is above zero, orange when it is zero but what it depends on exists (节点 added, none online), and grey while the count is unknown or there is nothing to have yet. Identity is not state: an avatar takes a soft colour of its own from the cover palette (its hue picked from the name, a 92% lightness wash under a 32% initial), roles and release channels are plain grey pills without a dot, and the line editor's hop labels (入口, 中转, 落地) are grey.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: A color, bar count or figure must describe reported state: an enabled resource, a published profile, a verified path, a line's historical probe and a live tunnel probe are separate facts. A line without a measurement shows no lit bars, a tertiary em dash and no unit; a line with unknown capacity says 负载未知 in tertiary rather than guessing a load color.

rules.name: The Shared Cover Rule
rules.body: A game wears one colour everywhere, and adding a game never recolours another. When a game is first stored, the control service gives it a cover slot one above the highest so far, inside the save transaction; edits keep the slot, and games stored before slots existed (and the built-in drafts) are backfilled in id order when the store opens and after seeding. The service sends cover_index (the slot minus one) to the administration's lists and the client's catalogue alike, and the admin's `Cover` and the client's `Palette.SteppedHue` both take the hue at that index in one nine-hue list (222, 340, 168, 22, 252, 140, 312, 192, 6) whose neighbours sit far apart. Only a game without an index falls back to a hash of its id. Region code badges are coloured by position in their own list (hues 205, 345, 155, 25, 270, 120 at 45% saturation and 42% lightness), so neighbours sit at least 100° apart in both apps; in the editor's suggestions a region not yet chosen is grey.

rules.name: The Instrument Figures Rule
rules.body: Every measured or coded value (milliseconds, percent, elapsed time, exit IP, region codes, the avatar initial, the version string) is set in Bahnschrift, and words never are. The unit follows the figure at label size in Ash Text, bottom-aligned, and disappears with the figure when there is no measurement. The administration follows the same rule for its counts and codes, and sets ids and hosts in Cascadia Mono.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Line Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by tone, not outline. An edge appears only to say something: an amber 1.5 DIP edge for selection, a field's hover or focus edge, a 12% white hairline around cover art. The administration keeps the rule with shadow in place of tone: no resting surface is outlined, and edges belong to controls (fields, secondary buttons, choices, switch rows) and to dividers inside a surface.

rules.name: The Probe Label Rule
rules.body: Two latencies exist and are never mixed or presented as in-game latency. Line rows show the control plane's historical line probe, captioned above the list "延迟为线路历史检测值", and the idle summary repeats it as "历史 38 ms" after the line name. The dial, the 延迟 tile, the library banner and the chart show the running session's current tunnel probe, captioned on the chart "当前隧道检测，约每 30 秒一次". Missing evidence is an em dash with its unit hidden; packet loss stays an em dash when the probe did not measure UDP. A stopped or new session clears the figures and the chart's history, and losing the local service replaces the pages with the disconnected state so no stale figure stays on screen.

rules.name: The Locked Session Rule
rules.body: While a session starts, runs or stops, everything that would change it locks: search, region tiles, line rows and refresh. The library stays readable: the running game's cover wears the green 加速中 badge, other covers dim to 55%, and clicking one raises a warning toast ("正在为 … 加速，停止后才能切换游戏"). Locked lists dim in place rather than turning stock white.

rules.name: The Refused Line Rule
rules.body: When the service refuses a start because of the line (full, withdrawn, node down), that line stays refused until the line list is refreshed (the refresh button beside 选择线路, or the library refresh) or three minutes pass: the row disables with a red load dot and "刚才无法使用，刷新后可重试", its latency becomes an em dash, the best remaining line is selected, and the red line under the dial names both ("… 暂时无法使用（cause），已切换到 …"), or says the region has no other usable line.

dos: **Do** preserve the light administration and dark native-client surface roles, and keep the administration framed in the client's graphite.
**Do** keep status labels, provenance, empty states, and errors visible beside the affected resource or action; in a form, under the field at fault.

**Do** let narrow web screens reflow rather than scroll sideways (a top bar and menu sheet at 860px, stacked row cards labelled by column at 720px), and keep a fixed hero over a scrolling game page at the client's minimum size.
**Do** use local Chinese-capable fonts: Microsoft YaHei UI for words and Bahnschrift for figures on both surfaces, and Cascadia Mono for ids and hosts on the web.
**Do** color every client latency by one scale (60 ms or less green, to 120 ms orange, above red) and light signal bars at 60, 100 and 160 ms.
**Do** draw new client icons as 24 px outline geometry at a 1.8 stroke with round caps, and regenerate brand rasters from the three-streak mark in `installer/make-brand-assets.ps1`.
**Do** give each new game a generated cover from the hue at its cover_index, the same in both apps, and colour region badges by their position in the list.
**Do** lead every admin list with an entity column (picture, name, sub line), put the row's next step first as its emphasised action, and keep destructive actions last, separated and red.
donts: **Don't** replace unknown counts or missing probe evidence with zero or invented healthy measurements.
**Don't** conflate a published rule, verified path, historical probe, and current connection.
**Don't** claim tested game compatibility or bundle proprietary game artwork without established evidence or assets.
**Don't** use amber to report quality or state on either surface, or a state tone as decoration; and don't bring back the retired cyan.
**Don't** outline resting surfaces: the client separates by tone and the administration by the Rest shadow; the Float shadow is for client layers above the page.

**Don't** pick a game's cover hue from list order or a hash when the service supplies cover_index, or renumber the slots of existing games; a game must not change colour between the two apps or when another game is added.
**Don't** edit in a centred modal or ask with the browser's confirm(); edits go in the side drawer, state changes through the risk-coloured confirm dialog.
**Don't** brand with a letter monogram; the brand is the three-streak amber mark, and first characters appear only inside generated covers.
